name: Greenland
prevalence_note: Grønlands Politi said on 20 November 2025 that it was receiving many approaches from people who had been sent a mail pretending to be a summons from Interpol-Europol and from the Danish national police leadership, used for extortion. GrønlandsBANKEN warned on 11 November 2025 of a Facebook profile using a Danish mortgage bank's name and logo to offer cheap loans, aimed especially at people in Greenland. In September 2026 both the bank and Naalakkersuisut warned of unsolicited Messenger contacts that impersonated the official contraception-compensation process. In October 2026, after an unauthorised access to civil-registration data that the government said included residents in Greenland, the bank told customers to be extra careful with unexpected calls, texts and emails, even if the sender already knew a name, address or civil-registration number.
cross_border_note: Several of the published cases borrow the names of Danish or international bodies (a mortgage bank, the Danish national police, Interpol-Europol, or the official compensation board that uses MitID). Greenland's own country code is +299; a Danish-looking sender or a familiar logo is not proof of a genuine Nuuk office.

scams.name: Extortion email pretending to be a police or Interpol-Europol summons
scams.name_en: Greenland Police, 20 November 2025: mails that pretend to be a summons from Interpol-Europol and from the Danish national police, allege a serious criminal investigation, and try to obtain money through fear
context_keywords: mail that names Interpol-Europol and Rigspolitiet
fake summons sent to an address in Greenland
threat of a serious criminal case
payment demanded to make the accusation go away

red_flag_keywords.text: this is a summons from Interpol-Europol, pay now
the national police chief has opened a case against you
pay this amount or the accusation will proceed
open the link in this official-looking police mail

scams.signals_en: On 20 Nov 2025 Greenland Police warned of extortion emails pretending to be Interpol-Europol and Danish police summonses alleging child abuse material. Police say they are scams: delete them, do not reply, click links or pay.
scams.legit_en: Greenland Police do not open criminal cases with unsolicited emails demanding payment or link clicks to answer a summons. Verify any genuine Greenland police contact via official politi.gl channels, never by replying.
bait_tactics: Do not reply, pay, or follow a link in a mail that claims to be a summons from Interpol-Europol or the Danish national police.
Delete the message, and if certainty is still needed, contact Greenland Police only through a channel published on the official Police site.
Warn close contacts, as the Police asked, so that the same extortion mail is recognised elsewhere.

scams.name: Facebook profile using a Danish bank's logo to offer cheap loans in Greenland
scams.name_en: GrønlandsBANKEN, 11 November 2025: a Facebook profile uses Nykredit's name and logo to offer cheap loans, directed especially at people in Greenland; the bank says neither Nykredit nor GrønlandsBANKEN contacts customers on social media
context_keywords: Facebook cheap loan aimed at Greenland
profile that copies a Danish mortgage-bank logo
request for bank details on Facebook

red_flag_keywords.text: cheap loan from this Facebook bank profile
send your details on Messenger to get the loan
Nykredit or the local bank wrote to you on Facebook
open this social-media link to apply

scams.signals_en: On 11 Nov 2025 GrønlandsBANKEN warned of a Danish Facebook profile using Nykredit's name and logo to pitch cheap loans in Greenland. Neither bank contacts customers on social media; never share data there or follow its links.
scams.legit_en: A genuine loan from GrønlandsBANKEN or from Nykredit is not arranged through an unsolicited Facebook profile. Those banks, according to the Nuuk bank's notice, do not approach customers on social media to collect personal or account data.
bait_tactics: Do not send personal or bank information to a Facebook profile that offers a loan, even if it uses a familiar Danish bank logo.
Do not follow the profile's links, and report the page to Facebook as the local bank advised.
If a loan is still needed, use only a channel the customer already knows from the real bank, not the social-media approach.

scams.name: Messenger contact impersonating the official contraception-compensation process
scams.name_en: Naalakkersuisut and GrønlandsBANKEN, September 2026: unsolicited Messenger or similar messages that pretend to handle compensation in the contraception case, then ask for personal data and later an account number
context_keywords: unsolicited request for an account number
claim to represent the official payout
MitID login only on the real compensation site

red_flag_keywords.text: we handle your compensation, send your details on Messenger
give your account number so the payout can be sent
share your MitID or SMS code in this chat
official compensation office wrote to you on Facebook

scams.signals_en: In Sep 2026 GrønlandsBANKEN and Naalakkersuisut warned of Messenger scammers posing as Spiralsagen compensation staff to steal personal data, account numbers and MitID/SMS codes. Real claims use Patienterstatningen with MitID online.
scams.legit_en: Naalakkersuisut confirms applicants are never contacted via Messenger about compensation. GrønlandsBANKEN notes real claims go through Patienterstatningen using MitID on its official site, not chats asking for account numbers or codes.
bait_tactics: End an unsolicited Messenger or Facebook approach that claims to handle the compensation, and do not send personal data, a civil-registration number, an account number or a MitID or SMS code in that chat.
If the person still needs to check a real application, use only the official Patienterstatningen route described by the bank, with MitID on that board's own site.
Say the messages can be raised with the real authority through published official contacts, not by continuing in the same thread.
